summary: Backend-only verification of the return_leg parity fix between GET /api/trips/{id}/timeline and GET /api/trips/{id}/route-geometry. (1) /app/backend/tests/return_leg_parity_test.py -> 3/3 PASS. (2) Independent verification script created a trip (has_return=true, home_location='Milano, Italia', stop 'Roma') and diffed both endpoints: key sets are exactly {home_location, home_coords, from_stop_id, transport_mode, geojson, distance_m, duration_s} on BOTH, and every value matched byte-for-byte including geojson, distance_m (572014.3) and duration_s (20244.5) - not just the required subset. Added a 2nd stop ('Firenze') and confirmed from_stop_id tracks the new last stop identically in both endpoints. (3) Regression: sprint_c(27)+sprint_ab(19)+trip_map(14)+trip_summary+orphan suites+parity = 83 passed after updating ONE stale assertion in sprint_c_test.py that still asserted the old buggy contract return_leg == {'home_location': ...}. Full tests/ dir: 294 passed, 21 failed - all 21 are the pre-existing phase5* / phase5b ORS_MOCK=0 failures already documented as known/out-of-scope in iteration_24 (mock-only city/km assertions return null with live ORS); none are related to the _build_return_leg import.

minor.issue: Pre-existing, unrelated: 21 phase5/phase5b/hotfix tests fail because ORS_MOCK=0 in backend/.env makes mocked-city km assertions return null (total_km=None). Same as iteration_24 known issue. Either set ORS_MOCK=1 for those suites or mark them mock-only.

critical_code_review_comments: timeline.py now imports _build_return_leg from map_routes.py, which imports geocode/_get_or_fetch_route - correct single source of truth, no cycle observed. Consider moving _build_return_leg into a neutral module (e.g. services/route_legs.py) so timeline no longer depends on a router module; the leading underscore also signals private API being consumed cross-module.

timeline.py builds coords_list = [None]*(n-1) + [last_coords] which relies on the builder only reading coords_list[-1]. If _build_return_leg ever reads earlier coords this silently breaks; a targeted signature (last_coords only) would be safer.
Optional: phase5* suites should be parametrised on ORS_MOCK so the 21 known failures stop masking real regressions in full-suite runs.

success_rate.backend: 100% (83/83 in-scope: parity 3/3, sprint_c 27, sprint_ab 19, trip_map 14, trip_summary + orphan suites)

seed_data_creation: Trips created and deleted in-test by dev-login users return_leg_parity@twt.app, return_leg_null@twt.app, return_leg_no_stops@twt.app, rl_verify_iter25@twt.app. All trips deleted at end of each test/script.
context_for_next_testing_agent: return_leg parity is fixed and fully verified (structural + value identity across both endpoints, with 1 and 2 stops, and null-parity for has_return=false and has_return=true+no-stops). sprint_c_test.py::TestTimelineReturnHome::test_return_home_day was updated by the testing agent to assert the NEW full-contract shape. Remaining 21 full-suite failures are ORS_MOCK=0 artefacts in phase5*/phase5b suites, pre-existing since iteration_24 - do not attribute them to timeline changes.
rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: timeline built its own minimal return_leg dict; fix delegates to map_routes._build_return_leg. The single regression seen (sprint_c_test test_return_home_day) was a stale test asserting the old buggy contract, not an app defect - assertion updated to the documented 7-key contract.
